misconception_description: Student believes that variable identifiers can only be one letter long.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekBilanganPrima
kamus
  n, i : integer
  p : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  if n < 2 then
    p <- false
  else
    p <- true
    for i <- 2 to n - 1 do
      if n mod i == 0 then
        p <- false
      endif
    endfor
  endif
  output(p)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes that all variable identifiers must be one letter long. Therefore, they renamed 'prime_num' to 'p' (for prime) and 'num' to 'n' (for number). The loop variable 'i' was already one letter so it remained unchanged. This makes the code less readable but doesn't affect its functionality. The student genuinely believes this is the proper way to write code and that longer variable names are not allowed.
